stem: An otherwise well child presents with petechiae; what broad coagulation study result would you expect?

options.text: Haemophilia is diagnosed in every child with petechiae
Factor XIII deficiency is specifically indicated

explanation: Normal coagulation studies are expected in an otherwise well child with petechiae. This presentation does not, by itself, indicate a specific coagulation disorder or confirm another diagnosis.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Correct because an otherwise well child with petechiae is described as having normal coagulation studies.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because petechiae in an otherwise well child do not imply a combined bleeding and thrombosis pattern.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because petechiae do not diagnose haemophilia in every child.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because factor XIII deficiency is not specifically indicated by this presentation.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because coagulation studies do not confirm non-accidental injury.
